paragraphs: Instance detection asks a system to find a particular object, identified through visual examples, inside a cluttered scene. This differs from recognizing an object category: the target is the specific instance. The paper addresses a shortage of sufficiently large datasets for studying this problem, which has received less attention than category-level object detection.

The authors introduce a dataset containing captures of 100 objects from multiple viewpoints and testing images at 6,000 by 8,000 pixels. Their training protocol combines these object captures with varied scene backgrounds. Pasting object images into scenes produces synthetic training examples whose bounding boxes are available from the construction process.

The benchmark also compares detection approaches. Combining the existing SAM segmentation model with DINOv2 features performs best, exceeding adapted end-to-end object detectors by more than 10 AP. Within this evaluation, that result shows the strength of combining general segmentation and learned visual representations, while providing a concrete reference point for future instance-detection methods.
neurips-2023-a-high-resolution-dataset-f.tldr: A new instance-detection dataset finds that combining SAM and DINOv2 outperforms adapted object detectors by more than 10 AP.

paragraphs: Real tabular datasets often contain many collected or engineered features, only some of which help prediction. Choosing a smaller informative subset can reduce overfitting. The paper argues that existing feature-selection benchmarks do not adequately reflect this situation: some use small curated feature sets, some rely on synthetic problems, and others do not judge selection by the performance of the eventual predictive model.

The authors build a benchmark around real datasets with additional extraneous features generated in multiple ways. Feature selectors are evaluated through the neural networks subsequently trained on their chosen inputs, including transformers. This makes the evaluation directly about whether selecting features helps the model that will actually use them.

They also propose a neural-network counterpart to LASSO based on input gradients. It outperforms classical feature-selection methods on challenging cases involving corrupted or second-order features. The contribution therefore combines a more practically motivated evaluation setting with a selection method that shows advantages within that setting.
neurips-2023-a-performance-driven-benchm.tldr: This benchmark evaluates feature selection by downstream neural-network performance and introduces an input-gradient method that improves selection on challenging feature sets.

paragraphs: Predicting whether an antibody binds a target requires examples that describe both the interacting molecules and the outcome. Existing public datasets can be small or lack non-binding examples and exact amino acid sequences. AVIDa-hIL6 addresses these gaps using VHH antibody domains obtained from an alpaca immunized with the human IL-6 protein.

The dataset contains 573,891 antigen–VHH pairs, with amino acid sequences and binding or non-binding labels produced by a new labeling method. The relatively simple structure of VHHs enables identification of full-length sequences through DNA sequencing. Including both outcomes gives learning methods examples of unsuccessful interactions as well as successful ones.

Alongside the original IL-6 protein, the dataset includes 30 artificially mutated variants. This supports studying how antigen changes affect antibody binding. Benchmark experiments indicate promise in existing machine-learning models, but also show that further work is needed to predict effective antibodies against previously unknown mutants. The resource makes that generalization problem an explicit target for evaluation.
neurips-2023-avida-hil6-a-large-scale-vh.tldr: AVIDa-hIL6 provides 573,891 labeled antigen–VHH pairs for studying antibody binding and generalization to mutated IL-6 targets.

paragraphs: A predictive model is more useful when it can indicate how much confidence its outputs deserve. Neural processes offer an approach to uncertainty estimation that combines qualities of Gaussian processes with the efficiency and expressive capacity of neural networks. Their adaptation to data containing multiple modalities, however, has received less careful study than their use with a single modality.

The paper introduces Multimodal Neural Processes, extending the neural-process framework with mechanisms designed for multimodal data. The central contribution is an uncertainty-estimation model that explicitly accounts for this setting. It addresses the challenge of assessing reliability when a prediction draws on several kinds of input.

Across extensive empirical evaluations, the method achieves reported state-of-the-art multimodal uncertainty performance. The experiments also show robustness to noisy samples, reliability in detecting inputs outside the training distribution, and faster computation than the compared leading method. These findings support its usefulness for assessing prediction reliability under the evaluated conditions, alongside its computational advantages.
neurips-2023-beyond-unimodal-generalisin.tldr: Multimodal Neural Processes extend neural-process uncertainty estimation to multiple modalities, with reported gains in robustness, detection reliability, and computation time.

paragraphs: Text-to-SQL systems turn natural-language requests into database queries. The paper argues that benchmarks emphasizing database structure with little actual content leave important practical challenges underexamined. A system working with large databases must understand stored values, handle messy content, connect questions to relevant external knowledge, and generate queries that run efficiently.

BIRD introduces 12,751 text-to-SQL pairs across 95 databases, totaling 33.4 GB and covering 37 professional domains. Its emphasis on database contents tests more than whether a model can translate a sentence into plausible SQL syntax. Successful queries must connect the user's meaning to what the database actually contains.

The reported evaluation places GPT-4 at 54.89% execution accuracy, compared with a human result of 92.96%. This gap demonstrates substantial remaining difficulty on the benchmark. The paper also analyzes query efficiency, highlighting that producing a correct answer and producing an efficient query are both relevant to database interfaces intended for practical use.
neurips-2023-can-llm-already-serve-as-a-.tldr: BIRD tests text-to-SQL on large, content-rich databases and reveals a substantial execution-accuracy gap between GPT-4 and humans.

paragraphs: Fluent language-model answers can contain factual errors, a particularly consequential problem in maternity and infant care. The paper targets two gaps in evaluating these errors: limited attention to long-form, knowledge-intensive answers and a strong emphasis on English. CARE-MI creates a Chinese-language benchmark focused specifically on this sensitive healthcare domain.

The benchmark contains 1,612 questions checked by experts and paired with references selected by humans. These materials provide a basis for assessing misinformation in extended responses. The authors also present a benchmark-construction approach intended to transfer to other domains requiring substantial factual knowledge and to languages with fewer evaluation resources.

Experiments find that the evaluated Chinese language models still have substantial shortcomings in maternity and infant care. To reduce the human effort involved in assessment, the authors supply ready-to-use judgment models for evaluating generated answers. They also compare evaluation approaches, making the contribution both a domain-specific test resource and an investigation into how automated assessment of long-form answers can improve.
neurips-2023-care-mi-chinese-benchmark-f.tldr: CARE-MI evaluates misinformation in Chinese maternity and infant-care answers using expert-checked questions and automated judgment models.

paragraphs: Diffusion generation repeatedly applies a learned model, so mistakes at one step can change the inputs encountered later. These accumulated errors can move generated samples away from the distribution used during training. Standard denoising score matching optimizes predictions on non-drifted data, leaving this mismatch between training and generation insufficiently addressed.

The authors add a consistency property requiring predictions on the model's own generated data to agree across time. Their theoretical analysis combines the equation describing this property with a conservative-vector-field condition. Together, these equations have a unique solution for a given initial condition. If denoising score matching learns the correct scores on non-drifted points, enforcing consistency can propagate those values to drifted points.

Experiments report improved generation quality on CIFAR-10, AFHQ, and FFHQ, including conditional and unconditional generation. The approach therefore connects a practical source of generation error to an additional training requirement. Its theoretical justification remains conditional on the stated initial-score and vector-field conditions, while the experiments demonstrate benefits in the evaluated image-generation settings.
neurips-2023-consistent-diffusion-models.tldr: Training diffusion models for consistency on their own generated data mitigates sampling drift and improves image-generation quality in the reported experiments.

paragraphs: Online algorithms must make decisions as information arrives, and learned predictions can help them anticipate what comes next. A useful prediction-assisted algorithm should perform close to the optimum when predictions are perfect while retaining strong guarantees when predictions are arbitrary. These two requirements are called consistency and robustness.

The paper studies a third requirement: performance should change smoothly as prediction error increases. Guarantees at the perfect-prediction and arbitrary-prediction extremes do not by themselves describe this intermediate behavior. The authors introduce a general property called discrete-smoothness to quantify how these guarantees fit together and use it to develop algorithms for online covering problems.

The resulting algorithms address set cover and facility location. For set cover, the contribution adds smoothness guarantees to earlier consistency and robustness results. For facility location, it also extends the treatment to nonuniform costs. Together, these results provide more informative guarantees about how prediction quality affects algorithm performance, covering the range between ideal and unreliable advice.
neurips-2023-discrete-smoothness-in-onli.tldr: Discrete-smoothness gives prediction-assisted set-cover and facility-location algorithms guarantees that vary smoothly with prediction error.

paragraphs: Many reinforcement-learning methods represent change in discrete steps, although the systems they control evolve continuously. This paper models those dynamics with nonlinear ordinary differential equations. It uses calibrated probabilistic models to represent uncertainty caused by limited knowledge, then applies optimistic exploration to guide learning about the system.

Continuous time introduces an additional decision: when to take measurements. The authors make this measurement-selection strategy explicit in their regret analysis. With Gaussian-process models of the dynamics, they establish sublinear regret for common measurement strategies, including equally spaced observations. Sublinear regret means the accumulated performance gap grows more slowly than the learning horizon.

The paper also proposes an adaptive strategy that chooses measurements using available data. Combined with Gaussian-process dynamics, it retains sublinear regret while requiring significantly fewer samples. Applications demonstrate benefits from continuous-time modeling and from adaptive measurement selection relative to the compared alternatives. The work thus treats observation timing as part of efficient exploration, alongside the choice of actions.
neurips-2023-efficient-exploration-in-co.tldr: A continuous-time reinforcement-learning method jointly addresses exploration and observation timing, with sublinear-regret guarantees and fewer measurements through adaptive sampling.

paragraphs: In-context learning uses examples supplied as context to guide a model on a task. Extending this approach to 3D point clouds creates a specific difficulty for masked modeling: point coordinates are themselves the tokens being hidden. Positional embeddings can also accidentally reveal information that should remain unavailable during prediction.

The authors introduce Point-In-Context, a framework that represents both task inputs and outputs as coordinates. This gives different point-cloud tasks a shared representation. They also introduce Joint Sampling, a module designed to work with the general point-sampling operator and address the masking and information-leakage issues that obstruct a direct extension from 2D methods.

Extensive experiments demonstrate the framework's versatility and adaptability across multiple tasks. With a more effective strategy for choosing prompts, it surpasses individually trained models in the reported comparisons. That qualification makes prompt selection part of the result: the demonstrated advantage depends on how contextual examples are chosen, alongside the framework's treatment of coordinates and sampling.
neurips-2023-explore-in-context-learning.tldr: Point-In-Context enables in-context learning for 3D point clouds through coordinate-based task modeling and a sampling module that addresses masking and leakage.

paragraphs: People adjust how they learn according to prior beliefs, decision urgency, and changes in their environment. Learning models, however, are often studied separately. This paper asks how different approaches can be situated within one mathematical framework, with the longer-term motivation of enabling agents to move between learning modes.

Generalized Belief Transport expresses learning through three constraints within unbalanced optimal transport. Different parameter choices recover models including Bayesian inference, cooperative communication, and classification. The authors visualize this parameter space as a cube, with familiar models occupying particular locations. They prove continuity and differentiability properties that provide a mathematical basis for interpolation between models.

The analysis also studies parameter limits, connecting boundary locations to learning models, and investigates long-run behavior and convergence mathematically and computationally. The paper documents learning under distribution drift and formulates conjectures about broader behavior. Its contribution is a structured relationship among learning approaches, with established properties and open questions explicitly forming different parts of that framework.
neurips-2023-generalized-belief-transpor.tldr: Generalized Belief Transport places several learning models in a shared mathematical space and establishes properties supporting interpolation between them.

paragraphs: Optimal transport studies how to move one probability distribution toward another while minimizing a chosen cost. For generative modeling, this can connect an easy-to-sample starting distribution to the data distribution. The paper addresses two difficulties with existing transport-based generators: sensitivity to outliers and challenges in optimizing the model during training.

The proposed generator uses a semi-dual formulation of unbalanced optimal transport. Its central change is to relax the strict distribution-matching constraint used in ordinary optimal transport. This changes how the model handles discrepancies between distributions. The authors also study a theoretical upper bound on the divergence between distributions under this formulation.

Experiments support improved outlier robustness, more stable training, and faster convergence. The model outperforms existing optimal-transport generators in the reported evaluations, reaching FID scores of 2.97 on CIFAR-10 and 6.36 on CelebA-HQ-256. These findings link a relaxation of the mathematical matching requirement to practical improvements in training behavior and generated-image quality.
neurips-2023-generative-modeling-through.tldr: A generator based on unbalanced optimal transport improves reported training stability, outlier robustness, convergence, and image quality.

paragraphs: Reasoning about an unfamiliar situation can require more than interpreting observations already available. A learner may need to propose an explanation, choose an experiment, observe its outcome, and revise the explanation. This paper introduces IVRE, an interactive environment designed to evaluate that cycle of reasoning under uncertainty.

IVRE contains varied scenarios centered on Blicket detection. Agents encounter ambiguous relationships between actions and effects and must determine the role of each object. They can actively gather information by testing their hypotheses. The environment encourages experiments that are both informative and efficient, and a game ends when uncertainty is resolved or the trial allowance is exhausted.

Evaluations reveal a clear shortfall for the tested artificial agents compared with humans. The result concerns the ability to use interaction to resolve uncertainty, making experimental choices part of the reasoning challenge. IVRE provides a concrete setting for investigating that weakness and for developing methods that better connect observation, hypothesis formation, and purposeful experimentation.
neurips-2023-interactive-visual-reasonin.tldr: IVRE tests whether agents can resolve ambiguous cause-and-effect relationships through experiments and reveals a substantial gap from human performance.

paragraphs: Image super-resolution learns to reconstruct a higher-resolution image from a lower-resolution input. Training commonly samples image patches uniformly, but image content is uneven: easy smooth regions dominate, while difficult edges and textures appear less often. The paper investigates how this imbalance affects learning and proposes changing the sampling process.

Bi-Sampling Parameter Attribution combines uniform sampling with inverse sampling. Uniform sampling preserves the original data distribution, while inverse sampling emphasizes difficult examples to improve their feature extraction. The method therefore maintains exposure to typical image content while giving harder reconstruction cases more attention during training.

The approach also uses integrated gradients to assess individual parameter contributions in models trained with the two sampling schemes. This attribution filters parameters with trivial contributions for further dynamic refinement, progressively separating parameter allocation to learn a more compact representation. Experiments on public datasets show improved performance for baseline super-resolution methods, supporting data resampling and parameter refinement as productive complements to architecture and optimization design.
neurips-2023-learning-re-sampling-method.tldr: BSPA improves image super-resolution by combining uniform and hard-example sampling with parameter attribution and refinement.

paragraphs: Learning every relationship in a large causal graph can be unnecessary when the goal concerns one particular outcome. With limited data, attempting the full graph can also identify variables that correlate strongly with the outcome without affecting it causally. The paper focuses causal discovery on the variables relevant to the chosen outcome.

The authors introduce necessary and sufficient causal graphs, whose variables are intended to be causal features of that outcome. Their approach uses probabilities of causation to assess feature importance and identify a relevant subgraph. They develop the NSCSL learning algorithm by establishing theoretical properties and connections between these probabilities and natural causal effects.

Studies on simulated and real datasets show NSCSL outperforming existing algorithms in the reported evaluations. The method also identifies crucial yeast genes associated with the target heritable traits through the proposed causal analysis. The contribution shifts the learning objective toward an outcome-specific causal structure, with theory guiding feature relevance and experiments supporting the resulting algorithm.
neurips-2023-on-learning-necessary-and-s.tldr: NSCSL uses probabilities of causation to learn outcome-specific causal graphs and outperforms existing algorithms in the reported studies.

paragraphs: Intracortical brain-computer interfaces can support communication, but neural recordings change over time. Maintaining decoding quality often requires users to interrupt communication and provide supervised recalibration data. This paper develops a way to update the decoder during use, addressing the practical burden of those repeated calibration sessions.

Continual Online Recalibration with Pseudo-labels, or CORP, uses language models to correct errors in the interface's text output. Those corrected outputs become pseudo-labels: automatically generated training targets for ongoing decoder updates. The communication stream itself consequently supplies information for recalibration without requiring a separate supervised collection session.

The authors evaluate CORP over 403 days with one clinical-trial participant performing an online handwriting task. It maintains 93.84% decoding accuracy and significantly outperforms the compared baselines. The paper presents this as the longest-running human iBCI stability demonstration and initial evidence for long-term plug-and-play communication. The single-participant scope matters when interpreting the result: it establishes sustained performance in this demonstrated use case.
neurips-2023-plug-and-play-stability-for.tldr: CORP uses language-model-corrected outputs to recalibrate a brain-to-text interface during use, maintaining 93.84% accuracy over 403 days in one participant.

paragraphs: A dataset carries a history: its sources, preparation steps, processing code, revisions, and subsequent uses. Machine-learning projects often capture this history poorly, leaving users with limited insight into how the data came to take its current form. The paper argues that this missing context can hide characteristics that affect downstream results.

Renku is a platform designed to make dataset preparation more accessible and dataset use easier to record and document. Its focus is the relationship between data and code across a project's lifecycle. Preserving that context helps make the work behind a dataset visible, including contributions that can otherwise be difficult to recognize.

The authors argue that such practices can encourage modifications to published datasets, support greater dataset diversity, and simplify trying alternative data sources. They illustrate Renku's benefits through projects spanning dataset creation, consumption, and presentation. The contribution is a platform and an accompanying case for sustainable data practices that support transparency, robustness, reuse, and appropriate credit.
neurips-2023-renku-a-platform-for-sustai.tldr: Renku helps document how datasets and code are created, changed, and reused to support more transparent and sustainable data science.

paragraphs: Classifier guidance steers diffusion generation toward a requested condition using gradients from a classifier. The paper identifies a problem with pushing too aggressively toward that condition: the process can suppress features shared with related classes. This can reduce sample diversity and encourage non-robust features that satisfy the classifier.

Progressive Guidance changes how the classifier influences generation over time. Early in sampling, while the image is still noisy, gradients from relevant classes contribute to building shared information. Later, the method progressively strengthens guidance toward the primary condition to refine image details. The sampling process therefore uses broader class information before emphasizing the requested distinction.

Experiments show improved image quality together with substantial diversity and robust features compared with ordinary classifier guidance. These results support the paper's argument that guidance should reflect the stage of image construction. Allowing shared information to contribute early can help preserve useful variation while later guidance directs the generated image toward its intended condition.
neurips-2023-rethinking-conditional-diff.tldr: Progressive Guidance uses related-class information early and target-focused guidance later to improve diffusion image quality, diversity, and feature robustness.

paragraphs: Constrained online optimization often uses projection to keep decisions inside an allowed set, but that operation can be expensive. Projection-free methods replace it with other optimization tools. This paper extends that idea to curved Riemannian spaces, where familiar Euclidean arguments become difficult because nontrivial affine functions are generally non-convex.

The authors develop methods for geodesically convex losses under two kinds of oracle access: separation and linear optimization. With a separation oracle, they obtain adaptive regret of O(T^(1/2)) with full information, O(T^(3/4)) with one-point bandit feedback, and O(T^(1/2)) with two-point bandit feedback. The guarantees therefore distinguish how much feedback the learner receives.

With a linear optimization oracle, the regret rates are O(T^(3/4)) for geodesically convex losses and O(T^(2/3) log T) for strongly geodesically convex losses. These sublinear guarantees mean accumulated regret grows more slowly than the number of rounds. The contribution establishes projection-free online learning guarantees on curved spaces under the specified loss and oracle conditions.
neurips-2023-riemannian-projection-free-.tldr: The paper establishes sublinear-regret projection-free online optimization on Riemannian spaces under specified oracle and geodesic-convexity conditions.

paragraphs: Contrastive learning can learn useful representations from unlabeled data, but strong performance has often depended on very large encoders. Compact models have been harder to train effectively with these methods. This creates a practical obstacle for applications where computation and energy budgets favor lightweight networks.

The paper introduces SACL-XD, combining Slimmed Asymmetrical Contrastive Learning with Cross Distillation. These components are designed together to support efficient self-supervised training of compact models. The method trains from scratch, avoiding the strong pretrained teacher required by relevant earlier distillation approaches. That removes an expensive prerequisite from the training setup.

Against the compared leading lightweight contrastive-learning and distillation algorithms, SACL-XD reports a 1.79% ImageNet-1K accuracy improvement for MobileNet-V3 with a 64-fold reduction in training FLOPs. The result demonstrates improved accuracy and substantially lower training computation in this comparison. More broadly, it supports designing the contrastive-learning procedure around compact models rather than relying on heavy encoders to obtain strong representations.
neurips-2023-slimmed-asymmetrical-contra.tldr: SACL-XD trains compact contrastive models from scratch, reporting improved MobileNet-V3 accuracy with 64-fold lower training FLOPs.

paragraphs: Off-policy evaluation estimates how a policy would perform using data collected by other policies. Fitted Q-evaluation does this by learning the evaluation policy's action-value function from a fixed dataset. This paper seeks to make that process more data-efficient by learning a representation of the dataset before applying fitted Q-evaluation.

The authors define a behavioral similarity metric for state-action pairs tailored specifically to off-policy evaluation. An encoder learns to represent this metric, and its transformed data become the evaluator's inputs. The theoretical analysis shows that the metric supports a bound on the resulting evaluation error, connecting representation learning to the quantity being estimated.

Experiments show that other similarity metrics can produce representations unable to express the evaluation policy's action-value function. The proposed representation improves data efficiency and reduces evaluation error relative to compared representation-learning methods on challenging tasks. It also substantially mitigates fitted Q-evaluation divergence under varying distribution shifts, supporting the value of tailoring similarity to the evaluation objective.
neurips-2023-state-action-similarity-bas.tldr: An off-policy-specific state-action similarity metric yields representations that improve fitted Q-evaluation efficiency, accuracy, and empirical stability under distribution shift.

paragraphs: Functional MRI records brain activity across space and time, producing data that are difficult to model directly. Approaches based on handcrafted features can discard useful information during extraction. SwiFT addresses this by learning from fMRI volumes end to end, allowing the model to work directly with their spatial and temporal structure.

The architecture adapts a Swin Transformer using four-dimensional windowed multi-head self-attention and absolute positional embeddings. These components enable processing of the high-dimensional volumes with attention to memory and computation efficiency. The authors evaluate predictions of sex, age, and cognitive intelligence using large resting-state datasets from HCP, ABCD, and UK Biobank.

SwiFT consistently outperforms the compared recent leading models in the reported experiments. Contrastive self-supervised pretraining further improves downstream performance, and an explainable-AI analysis identifies brain regions associated with sex classification. The work demonstrates an efficient route to direct spatiotemporal fMRI learning and presents it as a promising foundation for more scalable functional brain-imaging research.
neurips-2023-swift-swin-4d-fmri-transfor.tldr: SwiFT learns directly from four-dimensional fMRI volumes and outperforms compared models on sex, age, and cognitive-intelligence prediction.

paragraphs: Large generative language models can be difficult to deploy because of their size. Quantization-aware training addresses this by training with restricted numerical representations, but existing approaches can noticeably reduce accuracy. This paper examines ternary-weight models, whose weights use three possible values, and develops a training method intended to preserve their capabilities.

Token-scaled logit distillation transfers information from a teacher model while also using ground-truth training targets. The authors design it specifically for generative language models and report that it prevents overfitting while improving learning from both sources. The contribution focuses on how a highly quantized student is taught during training.

The paper reports an evaluation of large-scale ternary-weight language models with less than 1.0 degradation in perplexity. It also reports enhanced accuracy in common-sense question answering, arithmetic reasoning, and natural-language understanding. These findings support the feasibility of strong generative models under severe weight quantization in the evaluated settings, with distillation helping address the accuracy costs associated with that compression.
neurips-2023-token-scaled-logit-distilla.tldr: Token-scaled logit distillation supports large ternary-weight language models with less than 1.0 perplexity degradation and reported task-accuracy improvements.

paragraphs: Contrastive learning has become useful for extracting meaningful representations of neural activity, but its application to primary extracellular-data analysis has been less explored. The paper focuses on this earlier stage of analysis, including tasks such as spike sorting and cell-type classification, using high-density recordings of activity outside cells.

The authors introduce Contrastive Embeddings for Extracellular Data, or CEED. Their approach emphasizes careful choices of network architecture and data augmentations to learn useful representations. These design decisions adapt the contrastive-learning framework to the characteristics of extracellular recordings, with the aim of extracting broadly useful features for analysis.

Validation across multiple high-density recordings shows that the learned representations substantially outperform the specialized approaches used in the comparisons. The result supports the possibility of learning general representations that serve these primary analysis tasks effectively. The paper's contribution is both the CEED framework and empirical evidence that adapting contrastive learning to this data type can offer advantages over the evaluated task-specific methods.
neurips-2023-towards-robust-and-generali.tldr: CEED adapts contrastive learning to high-density extracellular recordings and learns representations that substantially outperform compared specialized approaches.

paragraphs: Some datasets contain examples with different numbers of dimensions, so generation must determine both the size of an example and its values. This paper introduces a model that learns those decisions jointly. Its generative process combines diffusion with jumps between spaces of different dimensionality.

The authors first define a forward process that adds noise while destroying dimensions. They then derive the reversed process, which creates dimensions as it generates data, and an evidence lower bound objective for learning an approximation to that process. Sampling runs this learned reverse dynamics to produce dimensions and state values together.

Experiments use molecular and video datasets with varying dimensionality. Compared with fixed-dimensional models that generate size and values separately, the proposed approach shows better compatibility with test-time diffusion guidance for imputation and improved interpolation. These findings suggest that explicitly coupling dimensionality and content can benefit tasks where generation must adapt both, rather than treating the number of dimensions as a separate modeling decision.
neurips-2023-trans-dimensional-generativ.tldr: Jump diffusion models jointly generate data values and dimensionality, improving reported interpolation and compatibility with guided imputation.
